sources: State-machine status guard with retired status codes (concept: transition guard must reject, never alias, retired codes)
Unit normalization through a factor table keyed by case-folded unit (concept)
Audit-trail completeness for GxP release records (concept: 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail, one entry per release)

defects.description: status_from_code(4) returns BatchStatus.SIGNED because _CODE_TO_STATUS maps retired code 4 (SIGNED_CODE_ALIAS). R1 requires ValueError. With batch status 4, signer != operator, quantity 1 unit mg, release_batch sets RELEASED and returns a record instead of raising ValueError.

_FACTORS['ug'] is MG_TO_UG (1000), so to_micrograms(2, 'ug') returns 2000 instead of 2; to_micrograms(2, 'UG') also returns 2000. R3 requires micrograms to equal the given microgram quantity, so release of 2 ug stores 2000.

defects.class: zero quantity raises wrong exception type
defects.description: release_batch(batch, signer, 0, 'mg', audit) raises TypeError('quantity must be greater than zero') because 'not quantity' is true for 0. R4 requires ValueError for 0. None still raises TypeError, which is correct.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: Idempotent early return: a RELEASED batch released again by the same signer returns the stored record before any status check or audit write, so no second audit entry is written (R5).
Status guard: only SIGNED passes, so RELEASED batches by another signer and REJECTED batches (R7) raise ReleaseError. The comparison is correct for R2 and R7.
Rejecting bool before the int check is correct: bool is a subclass of int and True would otherwise map to key 1 (DRAFT) silently.

Pre-existing, unchanged line in _write_audit: an OSError from the audit trail is logged and swallowed, so a release can complete without its audit entry. This is a real flaw on an unchanged line, outside the change; diff-mode review must not report it.
